submitted.rationale: Highest measured photocurrent: 3.24e-6 A at Fe0.26 Ni0.17 V0.56. Photocurrent rose steadily with V at low Ni: 1.72 µA at index 158, 2.8 µA at index 34, 3.24 µA at index 89. This fits FeVO4 (on the MACE hull, HSE gap 2.75 eV) plus V2O5 (gap 2.83 eV), both of which absorb at 3.2 eV. The Ni-substituted analogue is predicted to have a gap of only about 0.5 eV, so I kept Ni low.

rejected.reason: Measured 1.72e-6 A; the Fe-rich direction gives lower photocurrent
The Ni analogue of FeVO4 has a predicted gap of about 0.54 eV, so it is likely a poor photoanode

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts triclinic FeVO4 on the hull (0 eV/atom), and MEGNet gives an HSE gap of 2.75 eV, below the 3.2 eV photon energy, so it can absorb. Index 34 has near-1:1 Fe:V with the least Ni, so it should favour FeVO4 formation.

Supports keeping Ni low: the Ni-substituted FeVO4 analogue has a predicted gap of only about 0.5 eV, which suggests Ni-rich phases are metallic-like and recombine carriers. Index 158 is the most Fe-rich, low-Ni point (Fe 0.53, Ni 0.18, V 0.29), where I expect an Fe2O3+FeVO4 mix. It tests the Fe-rich direction away from index 34.

Support: V2O5 has a predicted gap of 2.83 eV, which still absorbs at 3.2 eV. Together with the stable FeVO4, a V-rich, low-Ni FeVO4+V2O5 region should stay photoactive. Going from index 158 to 34, photocurrent rose as V increased, so index 89 (V 0.56, Ni 0.17) extends that trend.
